key_insight: A graph neural network can be trained without labeled CFD data by minimizing finite-volume residuals on the mesh, yielding accurate thermo-fluid surrogate predictions.
engineering_relevance: This approach can cut the cost of generating training datasets for 3D coupled heat-transfer and fluid-flow simulations while preserving physics fidelity.
method: Build an attention graph neural network on the CFD mesh.
Train it by minimizing finite-volume residuals of the governing equations instead of supervised labels.
Evaluate against CFD references on steady and transient thermo-fluid benchmarks.
evidence_signal: Across four test cases, the FVM-loss model reached 2.3–2.8% all-field nRMSE on the two steady benchmarks and outperformed a data-supervised baseline on the two transient cases.
watch_item: Residual-based training may be sensitive to mesh quality, boundary-condition handling, and the choice of governing-equation discretization.
paper_title: Label-Free Finite-Volume-Residual Training of Attention Graph Neural Networks for Coupled Thermo-Fluid Fields
